title: Quantization Scouting Bulletin — Sprint 17 notes
content:
Sprint 17 — quick bulletin and raw notes (working doc)

Context and purpose:
- Objective this sprint: scout lightweight quantization techniques for new 13B family model we plan to onboard to Redwood Dedicated next quarter. Focus is on inference-quality tradeoffs at INT8/FP8 (hybrid) and practical knobs that integrate with runtime (packing, kv-cache friendliness).
- This doc is intentionally rough: contains bench snapshots, failed experiments, standup blurbs, and immediate follow-ups. Use as single-source ephemeral capture for the team.

Standup highlights (Mar 15)
- Priya: baseline runs completed for float16 vs int8-per-channel on dev subset (5k tokens total). Latency delta ~28% improvement for int8 at batch=1 on A100-40GB; however sample-level perplexity rose 1.9% on eval set.
- Ethan: tested KV-cache preservation with aggressive per-layer clipping; observed 0.6% additional loss but memory reduced 22% (static KV representation).
- Marta: PR for model conversion pipeline ready (w/scorecard export); needs review — conversion currently emits three quant artifacts: scale maps, zero_points, and per-head reorder map.
- Jonas: started A/B eval harness for hallucination rate on benchmark prompts (policy & math); early signal shows small bursts of incoherence when using mixed FP8 for attention-only layers.

Experiments (detailed)
1) Per-channel INT8 with symmetric quantization, 4-bit-like packing workaround
- Setup: per-channel for linear weights, symmetric quant, activation clipping with percentile 99.995. No per-activation calibration pass (we used running mean from calibration set).
- Results: throughput up 1.35x vs f16; token latency median down 22% on CPU path + GPU kernel savings. Quality: EM/QA on dev set drops 2.4% absolute; perplexity +2.1%. Failure modes: numeric instability on long-range position queries (>1024 tokens) — likely due to accumulation error in attention matmul kernel.
- Notes: this is promising for cache-heavy workloads where throughput matters; not great for strict quality SLA.

2) Hybrid FP8 for attention + INT8 for MLP (pack-friendly ordering)
- Setup: convert attention projection matrices to FP8 (E4M3), MLP dense to INT8 per-tensor. Preserve softmax/LayerNorm in FP16 to avoid scale blow-ups.
- Results: throughput ~1.18x, perplexity +0.8%. Hallucination spike observed in math prompts ~3x baseline (small absolute increase). Memory reduction modest (12%) but kernel-level speedups smoother.
- Next steps: try FP8 for Q/K/V only and leave out output projection to see hallucination correlation.

3) KV-cache packing tests (store packed int8 blocks)
- Setup: pack 32-token blocks into single GPU buffer; use lazy unpack only at attention compute.
- Results: memory reduction for long sessions (~>2k tokens) reached 30–40%; token tail latency increased by ~6ms due to unpack cost but batch throughput improved.
- Implementation notes: kernel-level unpack should be fused into attention compute to eliminate copy overhead; Jonas to prototype kernel change.

Benchmarks snapshot (dev harness, 1000 sample prompts, batch=1 unless noted)
- Baseline (FP16): median latency 94ms, PPL 8.1, hallucination rate baseline (policy prompts) 1.1%
- INT8 per-channel: median latency 73ms, PPL 8.27, hallucination 1.6%
- Hybrid FP8-attn/INT8-mlp: median latency 80ms, PPL 8.16, hallucination 3.3%
- Packed KV-int8 (long session sim): effective memory -35%, avg tail latency +10%

Quality checks and evals
- We ran the new eval harness (gh:GH-quant-bench-2027-03) against our standard prompt suite + new regulatory prompts (privacy leakage). No immediate leakage regressions, but two prompts produced incoherent token sequences under hybrid config — flagged for deeper case study.
- Need to extend evals to include: contrastive reranking sensitivity, top-k/top-p differences, and safety classification drift for quant configs.

Model onboarding checklist (short-term items)
- Finalize conversion pipeline PR (Marta) and add scorecard metadata fields: quant-config-id, calibration-set-hash, eval-run-id.
- Create a canary rollout plan: host both FP16 and preferred-quant variant behind a routing policy with automatic rollback at +2% hallucination or +3% PPL deviation.
- Add an e2e test for long-history sessions (>4096 tokens) to gating.

Open questions / unresolved
- How sensitive are our downstream rerankers to subtle distribution shifts introduced by FP8? Need to craft targeted reranker tests.
- Are we comfortable with hybrid configs that increase hallucination for certain math/policy prompts? What guardrails should runtime enforce (confidence-based fallback to FP16)?
- Kernel work: can we fuse unpack into attention in the current runtime without breaking batching semantics? SRE and runtime owners to advise on rollout complexity.

Immediate action items (owners)
- Marta: finish PR and add CI step to run conversion on toy model; due: 2027-03-19.
- Jonas: prototype fused unpack kernel experiment (simple CUDA prototype) and share microbench results; due: 2027-03-22.
- Ethan: extend eval harness with reranker sensitivity tests and add hallucination targeted suite; due: 2027-03-20.
- Priya: draft canary policy and automation playbook for quant rollouts; due: 2027-03-21.

Meeting note (sync w/ runtime & SRE 2027-03-16)
- Discussed deployment risk: kernel change requires coordinated rollout across Dedicated and Private infra to avoid heterogenous kernel versions causing OOMs. Plan: staged canary on dedicated with shadowing, then wider rollout.
- SRE asked for a metrics dashboard for: quant-variant traffic %, PPL delta 7-day moving avg, hallucination event rate. Product to review dashboard template.

Quick captures (informal)
- Idea: try per-head scale quant (instead of per-channel) for attention heads — could reduce head interference and help long-context numeric stability. Low-cost change to converter.
- Note to self: check PR history for FP8 exponent handling — earlier PR had small bug where exponent bias wasn't stored for fused matmul path.

Appendix (links and small logs)
- Dev-run logs: /mnt/dev-runs/quant/2027-03-15/ (internal path) — includes raw kernels + perf counters.
- Slack threads: #ml-quant (ref: thread ts 1678932100), #runtime-kernels (ask Jonas), #sre-ops (for rollout sync).
- Related PRs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/quant-research/pull/312 (conversion PR), https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/799 (packing API draft)

If you’re reading and have immediate pushback or quick wins (e.g., calibration dataset we should swap to), drop a note here or ping in #ml-quant. This doc will be archived to confluence once PRs land and plan finalizes.

— Priya (sprint lead, applied-ml)
